subject: Neurology
vignette: A 72-year-old woman with mild Alzheimer disease is started on donepezil. Her physician explains that this is a first-line treatment that increases cortical acetylcholine by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase. At follow-up she reports nausea, dizziness, and difficulty sleeping.
question: Which of the following best describes donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine?

options.text: NMDA receptor antagonists used for moderate-to-advanced dementia
First-line acetylcholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer disease; adverse effects include nausea, dizziness, and insomnia
VMAT inhibitors used to treat Huntington chorea
Agents that reduce glutamate excitotoxicity in ALS
Dopamine agonists used in Parkinson disease

explanation_correct: Donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine are acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and are the first-line treatment for Alzheimer disease. Their adverse effects include nausea, dizziness, and insomnia, and they are contraindicated in patients with cardiac conduction abnormalities.

explanation_incorrect.A: NMDA antagonism is the mechanism of memantine, used for moderate-to-advanced dementia.
explanation_incorrect.C: VMAT inhibition is the mechanism of tetrabenazine, used for Huntington chorea.
explanation_incorrect.D: Reducing glutamate excitotoxicity in ALS is the mechanism of riluzole.
explanation_incorrect.E: Dopamine agonists are used in Parkinson disease, not Alzheimer disease.

educationalObjective: Donepezil/rivastigmine/galantamine are first-line AChE inhibitors for Alzheimer disease causing nausea, dizziness, and insomnia.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 78-year-old man with moderate-to-advanced Alzheimer disease is started on memantine. His physician explains that the agent helps prevent calcium-mediated excitotoxicity by blocking NMDA receptors. At follow-up he complains of dizziness and confusion and reports seeing things that are not there.
question: Which of the following best describes memantine?

options.text: A first-line acetylcholinesterase inhibitor for mild Alzheimer disease
A VMAT inhibitor used for chorea
An agent that increases glutamate excitotoxicity in ALS
A peripheral COMT inhibitor used in Parkinson disease
An NMDA receptor antagonist for moderate-to-advanced dementia; adverse effects include dizziness, confusion, and hallucinations

explanation_correct: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist that helps prevent excitotoxicity mediated by Ca2+. It is used for moderate-to-advanced dementia, and its adverse effects include dizziness, confusion, and hallucinations, matching this patient's presentation.

explanation_incorrect.A: First-line AChE inhibitors are donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine, used in milder disease.
explanation_incorrect.B: VMAT inhibition is the mechanism of tetrabenazine.
explanation_incorrect.C: Riluzole decreases rather than increases glutamate excitotoxicity in ALS.
explanation_incorrect.D: Peripheral COMT inhibition is entacapone, used in Parkinson disease.

educationalObjective: Memantine is an NMDA antagonist for moderate-to-advanced Alzheimer dementia, with dizziness, confusion, and hallucinations.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 58-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (Lou Gehrig disease) is started on riluzole. His neurologist explains that the drug reduces glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity and has been shown to improve survival.
question: Which of the following best describes riluzole's mechanism and benefit in ALS?

options.text: Decreases neuronal glutamate excitotoxicity and increases survival
Inhibits acetylcholinesterase and improves cognition
Blocks NMDA receptors in moderate-to-advanced dementia
Inhibits VMAT and reduces chorea
Increases dopamine release in Parkinson disease

explanation_correct: Riluzole is used in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (Lou Gehrig disease); it decreases neuronal glutamate excitotoxicity and increases survival. The mnemonic is 'Treat Lou Gehrig disease with riLouzole.'

explanation_incorrect.B: AChE inhibition is the mechanism of donepezil/rivastigmine/galantamine for Alzheimer disease.
explanation_incorrect.C: NMDA antagonism in dementia is the mechanism of memantine.
explanation_incorrect.D: VMAT inhibition is tetrabenazine for Huntington chorea.
explanation_incorrect.E: Increasing dopamine release is amantadine, used in Parkinson disease.

educationalObjective: Riluzole decreases glutamate excitotoxicity and improves survival in ALS.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 45-year-old woman with Huntington disease has troublesome chorea. Her physician prescribes tetrabenazine. The pharmacology team notes that the drug inhibits the vesicular monoamine transporter, reducing dopamine packaging into vesicles and its release, and that it can also be used for tardive dyskinesia.
question: Which of the following best describes tetrabenazine's mechanism and clinical use?

options.text: NMDA receptor antagonism for Alzheimer disease
AChE inhibition for mild dementia
Reduction of glutamate excitotoxicity for ALS
VMAT inhibition decreasing dopamine vesicle packaging and release; used for Huntington chorea and tardive dyskinesia
MAO-B inhibition for Parkinson on/off fluctuations

explanation_correct: Tetrabenazine (and deutetrabenazine) inhibit the vesicular monoamine transporter (VMAT), decreasing dopamine vesicle packaging and release. They are used for Huntington chorea and tardive dyskinesia.

explanation_incorrect.A: NMDA antagonism for Alzheimer disease is memantine.
explanation_incorrect.C: Reducing glutamate excitotoxicity in ALS is riluzole.
explanation_incorrect.E: MAO-B inhibition is selegiline/rasagiline for Parkinson disease.

educationalObjective: Tetrabenazine inhibits VMAT, reducing dopamine packaging/release, and treats Huntington chorea and tardive dyskinesia.
